stem:
Ishita looks at the diagram. Straight lines $AB$ and $CD$ cross at $O$. The marked angle $\angle AOC$ is $72^{\circ}$, and $p$ labels the angle vertically opposite $\angle AOC$.

Which claim correctly gives the measure of $p$?

options.text: $p = 108^{\circ}$, treating an adjacent angle on a straight line as if it were the vertically opposite angle.
$p = 72^{\circ}$, because vertically opposite angles at the same intersection are equal.
$p = 72^{\circ}$, because the angles may be called opposite angles that must sum to $180^{\circ}$.
$p = 72^{\circ}$, only because $72$ is already printed near the crossing.

teacher.key_rationale: Vertically opposite angles at one crossing are equal, so p equals the marked 72°. Using an adjacent straight-line angle, renaming as opposite-that-sum-to-180, or grabbing the printed 72 alone all miss that equality test.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangle rods as crossing lines AB and CD at O with marked vertically opposite pair 72° and p.
